text: 64-year-old man with low-risk prostate cancer (cT1c, Grade Group 1, PSA 5 ng/mL), healthy, estimated life expectancy about 18 years. He chose radical prostatectomy. PSA 8 weeks after surgery is undetectable. Pathology: organ-confined, negative margins, no adverse features, 0/12 lymph nodes positive. What is the next step?
82-year-old man with low-risk prostate cancer (Grade Group 1, PSA 6), with heart failure and COPD; estimated life expectancy about 6 years. Asymptomatic. How should he be managed?

58-year-old man treated with external beam radiation therapy 4 years ago for low-risk prostate cancer; life expectancy >20 years. PSA nadir was 0.4; PSA is now 3.1 ng/mL on two measurements (above nadir + 2). What pathway applies now?

66-year-old man with low-risk prostate cancer, life expectancy about 15 years, underwent radical prostatectomy. PSA at 8 weeks is 0.3 ng/mL (never became undetectable). PSMA PET shows no distant metastases. What treatment is recommended?

79-year-old man who had radical prostatectomy 6 years ago; PSA had been undetectable and is now 0.4 and rising (PSA recurrence). He has severe heart failure with estimated life expectancy about 3 years, and no symptoms. What is recommended?

70-year-old man with PSA recurrence 3 years after radical prostatectomy; life expectancy about 12 years. PSMA PET shows two small bone lesions in the pelvis and no visceral disease. What is the next pathway?

68-year-old man with PSA recurrence 2 years after radical prostatectomy; life expectancy about 10 years. Imaging shows 9 bone metastases (spine, pelvis, ribs, femur) and two liver lesions. Castrate status not applicable (no prior ADT). What is the next pathway?
61-year-old man with low-risk prostate cancer, life expectancy about 25 years, chose active surveillance. Confirmatory biopsy 1 year later shows Grade Group 3 disease. What pathway applies now?
